Plutocratic

/ploo-tuh-KRAT-ik/ - the stress falls on KRAT · adjective

What It Means

Plutocratic means governed by the wealthy, with wealth itself holding the power.

The regatta's governing board turned plutocratic years ago — every rule change now waits on the pleasure of the three owners with the deepest keels and deeper pockets.

Worked Example

The gold-rush town's charter never mentioned wealth, but its politics were plutocratic from the first assay: the two men who owned the stamp mill picked the sheriff, and the sheriff collected their debts.

Plutocratic is more precise than 'rich' or 'corrupt' because it names who steers: wealth itself. A rich town isn't plutocratic until money starts writing the rules — and a plutocratic system can be perfectly legal, which is what its critics find most alarming.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

moneyed: simply wealthy; plutocratic means the wealth is holding the gavel

money-driven: steered by profit anywhere at all; plutocratic is specifically about who governs

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

classless: recognizing no rank by wealth at all

grassroots: power rising from ordinary people at the bottom

Where it sits · how far money reaches into power — unequal → privileged → plutocratic

unequal vs. plutocratic: An unequal society merely has gaps between rich and poor — a long way short of plutocratic, where the gap has been promoted into the government.

privileged vs. plutocratic: A privileged class enjoys the advantages money buys — schools, lawyers, second chances — but privilege stops short of plutocratic until wealth is openly steering the state itself.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — plut-

Root — plut-: wealth (Greek ploutos)

Root — -ocrat-

Root — -ocrat-: rule, power (Greek kratos)

Suffix — -ic

Suffix — -ic: characteristic of

Put it together

Put it together: Plut- (Greek ploutos, 'wealth') + -ocrat- (kratos, 'rule, power') + -ic = characteristic of rule by wealth. Greek gave the underworld's treasure-keeper the same root — Plouton, lord of everything under the soil — and the word keeps that glint: in a plutocratic order, whatever is being decided, the treasure decides it.

Use the root in a new word: autocrat

Use the root in a new word: autocrat: The board functioned well until its founder aged into an autocrat who canceled meetings and ruled by memo.

Root Check

Word Choice

critical / political

Plutocratic is an accusation with a definition behind it: wealth governs. Prefer it to vague words like 'corrupt' when the mechanism is money — bought seats, weighted votes, donor vetoes. Among its unit-mates, the first root decides everything: pluto- (wealth) versus theo- (god) versus olig- (few) versus merit (earned skill). Same -cratic engine, four different drivers.
